subject: Post-call recap + clarifying tokens vs requests vs cache
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <samantha@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T17:22:00-04:00
Subject: Post-call recap + clarifying tokens vs requests vs cache

Hi Samantha — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and three clarifying items so we can model cost properly for your initial proof-of-concept: 

1) Volume inputs we discussed: 250k monthly active end-users, ~1.6M generation requests/month estimated (based on your 6.5 requests/user/month) — see attached acme_usage_snapshot.csv.
2) Typical prompt shape: 1. short assistant prompt (system + user ~450 chars) + 2. short retrieval hits (avg 220 chars each) + 1. user follow-up (avg 80 chars). You mentioned you keep the retrieval result in the prompt rather than calling a separate embedding endpoint.
3) Business target: you want to budget ~$4000–$6,000 / month for model inference initially, and target $/1M tokens of roughly $X (we discussed aiming for $900–$1,200 per 1M tokens as a rough benchmark to compare).

Clarifying questions (helpful if you can confirm in reply):
- Are the retrieval snippets always included in the prompt (i.e., part of the generated input tokens) or do you cache/summarize them server-side and only send condensed IDs?
- Do you expect to cache prefixes between turns for the same user (session-level KV caching) or do you re-send the same prompt each request?
- Which percentile of responses do you care about for latency (p50 vs p95) — that affects the recommended batch/config.

I attached a quick workbook (RDW_unit_econ_workbook_v1.xlsx) with two pricing scenarios (hosted vs dedicated) and a simple tokenization example so the numbers line up. I also pulled your last 7 days of logs into acme_usage_snapshot.csv.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm whether retrievals are sent verbatim in the prompt (reply to this thread).
- We run a short sample (1k requests) through our hosted sandbox and show billed tokens vs characters vs requests.
- Marissa will follow with a draft MA/PO terms and estimated ramp pricing.

Thanks — Jordan

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + clarifying tokens vs requests vs cache

Jordan — added two quick notes from a pricing/ops lens: 

- Tokens vs characters: we should model both. Our billing runs on tokens (post-tokenization), not characters; rough rule-of-thumb: ~4 chars per token for English but that varies. The workbook has a tokenized example tab.
- Prompt caching vs billed tokens: if you can keep common prefixes in a KV cache (session or conversation-level) we can avoid re-sending those tokens to the model. However, billed tokens reflect what the model receives plus what it generates. So even if you dedupe on your side, anything in the request payload (after encoding) is billable.

For Acme specifically: if retrievals are stable per session, caching should cut billed tokens by ~20–40% depending on how much of the prompt is repeated. If retrievals change every request, caching helps less.

Also, Sam — for the sandbox run we'll need a short sample of 100 representative prompts and the server-side flow (where retrievals happen). If you can drop that into the Drive link, we can kick the test tomorrow morning.

—Marissa

Thanks Jordan & Marissa — appreciate the clear notes. Quick answers: 

- Retrievals: yes, for our current proof-of-concept we pass the top-3 retrieval snippets verbatim in the prompt. We do not yet have a session KV cache — every request rebuilds the prompt with recent context.
- Latency: our priority is p95 < 600ms for UI flows where users expect interactive feel. p50 is less important right now.
- Sandbox artifacts: I uploaded a 100-sample_prompts.json and a small extract of our retrieval outputs to the Drive folder you shared. Also attaching our internal monthly cost ceiling for POC: $5,500/mo.

On the $/1M tokens target: we're trying to understand how tokenization differences (characters -> tokens) will change the math. I noted your workbook but was surprised that requests are cheap but token-dense prompts make hosted pricing look expensive. Can you show a side-by-side of billed tokens vs request count vs character count for the same 100 samples?

Thanks — Sam
